hlni.insight: One unlabeled example does not prove which degree category it belongs to.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume one example defines an entire degree curriculum.
hlni.viewerChange: Recognize that isolated examples are insufficient for degree classification.
hlni.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification. NPV calculations are fundamental to both finance and management modules.
references: Corporate Finance fundamentals (common to both B.Com and BBA curricula)
hlni.payoff: The viewer moves from guessing to asking for the evidence needed to actually distinguish the programmes.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Evidence Gap
creativeAngle: A visual puzzle that challenges the assumption that single tasks define degree curricula.
objective: Teach students to identify missing information instead of relying on stereotypes when comparing degrees.
targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Challenge
shots.visual: A student looking at a tablet showing a complex financial spreadsheet.
shots.dialogue: Think B.Com and BBA are totally different? Let's test that.
shots.onscreenText: B.Com vs BBA: Guess the degree!

shots.name: The Evidence Reveal
shots.visual: Screen recording of a spreadsheet showing 'Example: NPV calculation for a project.'
shots.dialogue: Example: NPV calculation for a project. Is this strictly B.Com or BBA?
shots.onscreenText: Example: NPV calculation for a project.
shots.cameraPerformance: Direct screen capture, clear text focus.

shots.name: The Critical Question
shots.visual: Student looking back at camera, shaking head.
shots.dialogue: It's both. Stop guessing. What information would verify which degree this belongs to?
shots.onscreenText: What information would verify which degree this belongs to?

productionNotes.editing: Jump cuts between tablet and student.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a shared technical example to force the viewer to realize that one task doesn't distinguish between degrees, shifting focus to curriculum-wide evidence.

selected.title: The Missing Link Challenge
selected.audienceGap: Students assume one example defines an entire degree curriculum.
selected.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
selected.viewerChange: Recognize that isolated examples are insufficient for degree classification.
selected.concept: A visual puzzle where an example is presented and the viewer must guess the degree, only to be told the evidence is missing.
selected.device: A 'Guess the Degree' game that forces a 'Not enough info' conclusion.
selected.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification.
methodSteps: Present one example without a source linking it to a category.
Separate a plausible guess from what the available information proves.
Identify the exact missing source or information needed to decide.
selected.interpretationRule: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.visibleProof: A forced-choice guess is replaced by a justified third answer and a precise request for missing evidence.
selected.payoff: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.limitations: Do not assert that the example belongs to both degrees, or to either one, without actual curriculum evidence.

demonstration.input: A screenshot of a spreadsheet calculation.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: NPV calculation for a project.
demonstration.observation: The viewer realizes the calculation occurs in both accounting and management contexts.

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: A split-screen view: one side shows a vague task, the other shows the three-column audit grid.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
